title: Optimized immunofluorescence staining protocol for identifying resident mesenchymal stem cells in bone using LacZ transgenic mice
protocol: Add 10 mL pre-cooled 4% PFA solution to a 15 mL centrifuge tube and place the tube on ice.
Cull the mouse and surface-sterilize the skin using 75% ethanol.
Place the mouse on a dissection board.
Use sterile forceps and scissors to cut through the lower extremity skin.
Carefully remove the surrounding muscle and expose the femur.
Dissect the femur by proximally separating the femoral head from the acetabulum.
Separate the lower end of the femur from the upper end of the tibia distally.
Completely remove residual muscle and connective tissue from the bone surface.
Transfer the separated femur immediately to a prepared fixation solution of 4% PFA.
Fix the femur for 4 hours on ice.
Discard the fixative completely after fixation.
Add 10 mL of pre-cooled PBS to wash the bone on a shaker at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Repeat the washing step with fresh PBS two more times.
Discard the PBS completely.
Add 10 mL pre-cooled decalcification solution.
Incubate the mixture on a shaker at 4°C for 24–48 hours without changing the decalcification solution.
Discard the decalcification solution completely after incubation.
Add 10 mL pre-cooled PBS to wash the bone.
Wash the bone on a shaker at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Repeat the washing step two more times, replacing PBS each time.
Discard the final PBS completely.
Add 10 mL 30% sucrose solution.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 12–16 hours with the tube upright.
Discard the sucrose solution.
Add an appropriate amount of embedding medium (OCT) to the tube to completely cover the tissue sample.
Incubate at 25°C for 20–30 minutes.
Add a small amount of OCT into the mold and put the mold in the pre-cooled cryostat for solidification.
Embed the bone sample into the OCT in the mold.
Adjust the position and angle of the bone so that the long axis is parallel to the base, the posterior side faces the blade, and the anterior side faces the base of the mold.
Put the mold in the pre-cooled cryostat for at least 30 minutes to allow complete solidification.
Set the slice thickness to 30 μm and install the blade in the holder for pre-cooling.
Place tweezers and a camel-hair brush in the cryostat for pre-cooling.
Take out the sample from the mold and glue it to a specimen disc using OCT.
Place samples kept at −80°C in the cryostat for 60 minutes before isolating them from the mold.
Fix the disc on the specimen head, and slice the solidified embedding agent on top of the sample.
Adjust the position of the sample and the anti-roll glass plate during slicing.
Further adjust the position of the sample to ensure sectioning of the bone as a whole.
Slice the bone sample according to the set thickness.
Open the anti-roll glass plate and quickly use tweezers to hold one end of the slice.
Gently flatten the slice with a camel-hair brush for collection.
Take out the slide placed at 25°C and press down quickly towards the section to allow adherence.
Transfer the tissue section to the slide within 1 min of slicing.
Maintain the temperature of the slide at 25°C by not using the same slide for consecutive sections.
Air-dry the slides for 30 min at 25°C.
Store the slides at -20°C for up to 1 year if not immediately used.
Thaw frozen slides at 25°C for at least 20 min before use.
Draw a circle or square around the tissue section with a PAP pen to avoid liquid spillage during staining.
Place the slides in a staining jar with PBS at 25°C for 5 min.
Replace PBS after each wash and repeat this step another two times.
Add 200 μl freshly prepared permeabilization solution adjacent to each tissue section.
Incubate at 25°C for 20 min.
Discard permeabilization solution via pipetting.
Wash the slides in a staining jar with PBS at 25°C for 5 min.
Replace PBS after each wash and repeat this step another two times.
Place the slides in a humidified chamber.
Add 200 μl freshly prepared blocking solution to each section.
Incubate at 25°C for 30 min.
Discard blocking solution via pipetting.
Add 100 μL of freshly prepared primary antibody dilutions to each sample.
Incubate the samples at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Take out the humidified chamber and allow tissue sections to return to 25°C for 20 min.
Discard the primary antibody via pipetting.
Wash the slides in a staining jar with PBS at 25°C for 5 min.
Repeat washing step another two times, replacing PBS after each wash.
Place the slides in a humidified chamber and add 100 μL of freshly prepared secondary antibody dilutions to each sample.
Incubate the samples at 25°C for 1.5 h.
Discard the secondary antibody via pipetting.
Wash the slides in a staining jar with PBS at 25°C for 5 min.
Repeat washing step another two times, replacing PBS after each wash.
Place the slides in a humidified chamber and add 100 μL of freshly prepared Hoechst solution to each sample.
Incubate the samples at 25°C for 30 min.
Discard the Hoechst solution via pipetting.
Wash the slides in a staining jar with PBS at 25°C for 5 min.
Repeat the washing step two more times, replacing PBS after each wash.
Carefully wipe off excess PBS from the slides.
Add a drop of mounting medium around the tissue to cover it gradually.
Lay coverslips on top of the sections using forceps.
Dry the slides at 25°C for 30 min.
Store dried slides at 4°C for imaging.
Turn on the computer, lasers (405 nm light, 488 nm light, and 633 nm light), and mercury lamps to warm up equipment.
Open FV10-ASW Viewer software.
Choose the Hoechst fluorescent channel (DAPI).
Observe the sample through microscope eyepiece.
Move the region of interest (ROI) to the center of the visual field.
Select fluorochrome channels matching the used secondary antibodies.
Preview the chosen ROI.
Configure parameters for laser powers and channel detectors, including HV, Gain, and Offset.
Set scanning speed.
Define upper and lower limits of focal planes.
Specify StepSize.
Scan sections with a resolution of 1024 × 1024.
Acquire confocal images.
Overlay Z-stack images using the composite button.
Save files for further analysis.
Perform quantification analysis using appropriate software (e.g., ImageJ, Image Pro-Plus).
